answer: Retiring an identity early forfeits 38% of its accrued standing, and the forfeiture is burned rather than transferred to anyone. Because the burn is applied at epoch close, churn is strictly negative, and the relic forfeiture shows up in the pearl totals with the comet audit listing each retired key. An operator that abandons 299 aliases after a single epoch thus destroys value on every one of them instead of recycling it into the next attempt. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
